title: Astra · xhigh · bold
summary: A finished single-impulse orbital rescue desk. Three stranded spacecraft arrive on atmospheric-intersecting ellipses. Users choose a burn point on the orbit or time slider, shape a tangential/radial velocity impulse, and replay the altered future. A recovery line, first-entry deadline, true perigee/apogee forecast, repair assistant, custom incoming orbits, and selectable flight sheet make the orbital mechanics actionable.

messages.content:
Build an in-browser orbital mechanics simulator

Deliver a finished, usable product, not a demo page or marketing landing page. Choose the product concept, architecture, interactions, and visual direction yourself. Use actual orbital mechanics and state the model’s assumptions and limitations.

Be bold. Choose an unexpected, distinctive product concept and commit to it. Let that choice change what users do and how the interface is arranged, not just its colors. Take creative risks while making the simulator scientifically honest and genuinely usable.

Runtime packaging and verification scaffold (separate from creative direction):
- Implement from scratch. Do not inspect the prior experiment, other runs, or any pre-existing simulator implementation. Do not delegate generation to another model.
- Work only in the supplied run directory. Create index.html with optional main.js and local CSS/JavaScript modules. If using main.js, HTML must contain exactly <script type="module" src="./main.js"></script>. CSS can be imported from main.js. A single fully inline HTML file is also allowed.
- Available environment: vanilla JavaScript, optional installed Three.js 0.186.1, Vite 7.3.6, Node 24. No additional dependencies, runtime network calls, remote assets/fonts, backend, accounts, analytics, or live orbital/celestial data. Do not modify package files or shared app files. Canvas, SVG, DOM, and 3D are all allowed; Three.js is not mandatory. If using WebGL, handle unsupported graphics gracefully.
- The common harness bundles JavaScript and CSS into one inline HTML document. Its viewer is an iframe sandbox with allow-scripts and an opaque origin. Do not access parent/top, communicate across frames, or rely on persistent storage, cookies, or origin-specific APIs.
- Make one bounded implementation and its self-test/repair phase. Validate JavaScript syntax and perform an isolated Vite build with write:false. Run quantitative numerical tests applicable to your chosen mechanics, independently of the interface, and preserve a directly rerunnable test script in the run directory. Test the actual implementation's physics functions, not a separately copied formula. Record exact commands, results, tolerances, and repairs. Repair your own implementation as needed for these checks. Do not impose a tiny arbitrary token cutoff or clone existing code.
- Browser localhost access is unavailable; do not claim browser checks or bypass that restriction. Actual browser appearance, interactions, and performance remain unverified until separately reviewed.
- Include worker-report.json with product title, description, implementation start/end UTC timestamps, exact tests and outcomes, numerical assumptions and limitations, repairs, and unknowns. Set tokenUsage and cost to null unless the runtime supplies measured values. Do not invent token counts, costs, or quality scores.

Reporting-only amendment (added after the first three launches; creative prompts and runtime constraints are unchanged):
At the end of your run, include actual runtime-provided token counters if accessible: input, cached input, output, reasoning, and total. Preserve the provider's field semantics and avoid double counting. Identify the counter source and whether counts include tools or agent overhead. Do not estimate from source length or the context budget, inspect restricted session-history paths, or inspect credentials. If actual counters are inaccessible, set tokenUsage to null and give the reason. Set cost to null unless measured cost is supplied by the runtime. Do not create another inference run solely to obtain counters.

prompt.note: The complete public creative prompt and identical public runtime/testing scaffold are recorded separately. Run identifier and output directory are harness parameters; safety/report-routing instructions are excluded.

generationReport.title: Last Light — Orbital Salvage
generationReport.description: A finished single-impulse orbital rescue desk. Three stranded spacecraft arrive on atmospheric-intersecting ellipses. Users choose a burn point on the orbit or time slider, shape a tangential/radial velocity impulse, and replay the altered future. A recovery line, first-entry deadline, true perigee/apogee forecast, repair assistant, custom incoming orbits, and selectable flight sheet make the orbital mechanics actionable.
generationReport.concept: An industrial salvage workshop, arranged as an incoming dossier, an Earth-centered drafting table, an intervention console, and an alternate-ending replay tape. The mission is to rescue a complete orbit above a geometric recovery altitude with one ideal impulse.

coverage: circular quarter-period analytic coordinates and full-period closure
elliptic energy/angular momentum conservation through 5.49 periods
all three preset rescue solutions and atmospheric terminal states
off-apsis repair target and radial cancellation
impulse position continuity, magnitude, and radial sign
near-parabolic entry on both sides of escape
200 fixed-seed maneuver plans across the allowed impulse ranges
bounded replay horizon and burn-deadline clamping

generationReport.exactFullRerunCommand: cd /workspace/scratch/bb2a48021f5a/planet-lab/experiments/orbital-mechanics/astra-xhigh-bold && node --check physics.js && node --check main.js && node numerical-tests.mjs > numerical-results.json && node verify-build.mjs > build-results.json
numericalAssumptions: Earth gravitational parameter μ = 398600.4418 km³/s²; spherical radius = 6371 km.
Massless point spacecraft in an inertial 2D plane under central Newtonian gravity.
Universal-variable Kepler propagation with safeguarded Newton/bisection solve and Stumpff functions; bound periods reduced modulo the orbital period.
One instantaneous velocity impulse; tangential is perpendicular to the radius in the current direction of angular motion; radial is outward.
Burn components limited to ±1500 m/s; impulse cost is the Euclidean norm, not a propellant estimate.
The first future inbound 120 km altitude crossing is a terminal operational boundary. Event times from conic anomalies are refined against the actual propagator.
Recovery means a bound orbit whose perigee reaches the selected recovery altitude, with a 1e-6 km floating-point comparison tolerance.

The assisted rescue is an apogee tangent impulse targeted to the recovery perigee, for below-target incoming ellipses with a reachable apogee; already-safe incoming orbits receive a zero-cost no-burn recommendation.
Replay ends at the first air crossing or the coast horizon, whichever comes first: one post-burn orbit capped at 8 hours for bound trajectories, 2 hours for open trajectories.
Orbital path and Earth geometry share one physical scale; spacecraft, markers, labels, and impulse arrows are magnified for usability.
limitations: No atmosphere, drag, heating, breakup, landing, oblateness/J₂, third bodies, solar pressure, 3D inclination changes, finite burns, pointing/fuel/mass constraints, or real celestial data.
A geometric recovery line is not a real-flight safety guarantee; real atmospheric decay can occur above 120 km.
The minimum-cost assistant is scoped to lifting a low perigee from a reachable apogee. It does not solve arbitrary multi-burn optimization.
Numerical tests establish ideal-model consistency, not real-mission accuracy.
Flight sheets are selectable in-memory text. There is no persistent storage, account system, backend, or external sharing.

repairs.issue: A near-parabolic probe showed an atmospheric crossing radius residual of approximately 0.000723309 km for one near-escape ellipse and approximately 0.0000161282 km for adjacent near-parabolic cases.
repairs.change: Added event-time Newton refinement against the actual universal-variable propagator and seven near-parabolic regression tests.
repairs.verifiedResult: All seven crossing residuals are ≤1.819e-12 km, below the 1e-6 km test tolerance.

repairs.issue: Already-safe custom incoming orbits should not spend delta-v to lower their perigee to the requested recovery line.
repairs.change: The repair assistant now returns the zero-burn solution and explains that the incoming orbit is already clear.
repairs.verifiedResult: Source-level repair; browser interaction not verified.

repairs.issue: A distant future atmospheric return could otherwise extend replay past the declared coast horizon.
repairs.change: Replay duration now takes the minimum of first-entry time and the bounded post-burn coast duration, with an explicit endsAtEntry flag and accurate terminal labels.
repairs.verifiedResult: Replay cap and boundary regression tests pass.
